items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I used to go there around 11 o'clock... Bix would sit down there, but oh, he'd play beautiful piano.

ctx.x: Yeah, Jimmy McPartland was the trumpet player. It was sounding good.

Yeah, Pee-wee, Pee-wee's nose, really, really russling the mind. Is he? Yeah, Pee-wee, when I first went to New York, he was doing a lot of recording with Nichols and those guys. Yeah, yeah. And then the other time, he and Bix were living together.

And they only stayed a month. Because they got in the, uh, Hardy wasn't in the union. Chink wasn't in the union. I think Skagliona was the only one that was in the union. Well, uh, they had to join the union up there. Well, they had, uh, no, I think, uh, they went to Florida. I think they went to Pensacola or something like that. Where you could join the union for a full five dollars. And join before they went up there. Anyway, they got messed up with the union somehow. Uh, with, uh, Petrillo then was, was, uh,…

They had to play the same thing for each one of them, but the only thing was that Chink played it too good. He didn't even put a little bit of his own in there. That wasn't on the paper, you know. And the piano player looked up at him, but anyway they smoothed it. They only worked a month with the Rhythm Kings until the Union threw the four of them out and they came back home. But Bix had come to Chicago in the meantime and he used to come in and ask him to let him sit in. And Paul Moriz and Rapp used to fluff…
